bib.title: Artificial Artificial Artificial Intelligence: Crowd Workers Widely Use Large Language Models for Text Production Tasks

read.skipped: none; 9 pages, no appendices; references skimmed

question: To what extent do crowd workers on MTurk use LLMs when completing a text production (abstract summarisation) task?
hypothesis: Crowd workers have financial incentives to use LLMs, so a substantial share of crowdsourced text is likely LLM-produced.
contributions: Case study estimating 33-46% of MTurk summaries were produced with LLM help
A bespoke, low-cost synthetic-text detector (fine-tuned e5-base) that beats off-the-shelf detectors on this task
Post-hoc validation using keystroke/paste logs and overlap with the source abstract

method.summary: Reran a single-step abstract summarisation task from Horta Ribeiro et al. (2019) on MTurk, logging keystrokes. Fine-tuned an e5-base classifier on human vs ChatGPT-written summaries of the same task, applied it to the 46 new summaries, and validated with paste and longest-common-substring heuristics.
method.task: crowd-sourced abstract summarisation; synthetic-vs-human text classification

eval.protocol: Two train/test splits (abstract-level, summary-level); +/- values in Table 1 not defined; 95% CIs on prevalence (method not stated); post-hoc validation via paste logging: summaries with no paste assumed human (false-positive check), pasted summaries with low overlap assumed synthetic (false-negative check).

prompts.purpose: worker task instructions (ChatGPT prompt used the same instruction; exact text not given beyond Fig 2)
prompts.text: You will be given a short text (around 400 words) with medicine-related information. Your task is to: Read the text carefully. Write a summary of the text. Your summary should: Convey the most important information in the text, as if you are trying to inform another person about what you just read. Contain at least 100 words. We expect high-quality summaries and will manually inspect some of them.

limits: One task (summarisation), one platform, 46 summaries from 44 workers, one time point (June 2023); authors flag generalisation to harder tasks as uncertain
Authors call it work in progress

Detector trained only on ChatGPT output; prevalence depends on threshold choice and the classifier-on-human distribution shift; validation uses assumptions (no paste = human, low-overlap paste = synthetic) not ground truth
Only 5 no-paste summaries underpin the false-positive check; 'paste' does not confirm LLM use
No error bars defined; hardware, optimizer and seeds not stated
Keystroke tracking raises privacy concerns (authors' ethical note)
